# Cadia, 2018

## 1. Setup

```{r}
# Load packages

library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(MASS)
library(factoextra)
library(gridExtra)
library(cluster)

set.seed(1234)
```

## 2. Prepare Data

**Prepare data to compute distance matrix:**

- Read data and extract only displacement columns

- Check for missing fields

- Summary statistics

```{r}
# Filter and prep data

cadia <- read_excel("cadia_2018_ps.xlsx")

str(cadia)
head(cadia)
dim(cadia)
names(cadia)
```

```{r}
# Extract displacement columns
d_cols <- grep("^D_", names(cadia), value = TRUE)
length(d_cols)
head(d_cols)

X <- cadia[, d_cols]

head(X)

dim(X)

# Check for missing vals

sum(is.na(X))
```

## 2. EDA

- Plot single time series points

- Sample roughly half the points (total 45) and plot them together

- Plot the mean displacement over time

```{r}
# Plot 3 points
# example to show how each point may act sporatically or very differently to others

par(mfrow=c(1,2))

plot(as.numeric(X[1, ]),
     type = "l",
     xlab = "Time index",
     ylab = "Displacement",
     main = "Example time series")

plot(as.numeric(X[2, ]),
     type = "l",
     xlab = "Time index",
     ylab = "Displacement",
     main = "Example time series")

plot(as.numeric(X[3, ]),
     type = "l",
     xlab = "Time index",
     ylab = "Displacement",
     main = "Example time series")

plot(as.numeric(X[4, ]),
     type = "l",
     xlab = "Time index",
     ylab = "Displacement",
     main = "Example time series")

# Make axis same !
```

```{r}
# Sample the data to select smaller # of rows
set.seed(1234)
sample_rows <- sample(1:nrow(X), 10)

# colours for each line
cols <- rainbow(length(sample_rows))

plot(as.numeric(X[sample_rows[1], ]), type = "l", xlab = "Time index", ylab = "Displacement",
     main = "Sample time series",

for (i in 2:length(sample_rows)) {

}

# heave vs settling
```

```{r}
# mean displacement over time

plot(colMeans(X), type = "l", ylab = "Mean displacement", xlab = "Time index", main = "Mean displacement over time")
```

## 3. Hierarchical Clustering

**Convert data to matrix and remove zero-variance columns**

```{r}
# Matrix

X <- cadia[, d_cols]
X_matrix <- as.matrix(X)

sum(is.na(X_matrix))

```

```{r}
# baseline date = 1st column

col_sd <- apply(X_matrix, 2, sd)

which(col_sd == 0)

```

```{r}
# Remove first column (0 = baseline date of cumulative displacement)

# Remove zero-variance columns from clustering input
col_sd <- apply(X_matrix, 2, sd)

zero_cols <- colnames(X_matrix)[col_sd == 0]
zero_cols

X_matrix_cluster <- X_matrix[, col_sd > 0, drop = FALSE]
```

- Explanation on why I removed the column:

**Compute distance matrix**

```{r}
# Distance Matrix
  # distance measure: for now Euclidean
      # test against others later

d_mat <- dist(X_matrix_cluster, method = "euclidean")
```

- distance matrix explanation

**Run cluster analysis**

```{r}
#### Run the cluster analysis ####

fit <- hclust(d_mat, method="ward.D2")
```

- Ward linkage method chosen: Minimises the total within-cluster variacne and finds the pair of clusters that leads to minimum increase in total within-cluster variance after merging

```{r}
# Plot the clusters

plot(fit, labels = FALSE)
rect.hclust(fit, k=4, border="darkred")
```

```{r}
plot(fit, labels = FALSE)
```

- Dendrogram can be used to help determine the number of clusters:
  - The y-axis represents the linkage distance at which clusters are merged.
  - In Ward's method:
    - A low height means 2 obs/clusters are very similar
    - A high height means two clusters are quite different
- A cut corresponding to 4 clusters was selected initially as it occurred before a substantial increase in linkage distance.

### 4.1 Assign Clusters to Data

```{r}
# Split into k clusters
cluster_d_4 <- cutree(fit, k=4)
table(cluster_d_4)
```

```{r}
# Assign cluster IDs
cadia$cluster_id <- cluster_d_4
```

```{r}
nrow(cadia)
length(cluster_d_4)

table(cadia$cluster_id)
```

### 4.2 Export for ArcGIS

```{r}
write.csv(cadia, "cadia_cluster_4_unscaled.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5. K-Means Clustering

- Can use the same pre-processing as the hierarchical version for easy portability.

#### Choosing k:

1.  Elbow method

```{r}
fviz_nbclust(X_matrix_cluster, kmeans, method = "wss")
```

- Within-cluster sum of squares measures the total variance within a k-means cluster, overall quantifying how close data points within a cluster are to the cluster's centroid.

- The total within-cluster sum of squares is what we aim to minimise by performing k-means clustering. The elbow method examines the relationship between the number of clusters and the within-cluster sum of squares (WCSS).

- The elbow method systematically experiments with different numbers of clusters (k) from 1 to 10, where at each k value, the WCSS is plotted.

- WCSS always decreases as k increases, however, the improvement is only substantial up to a certain point, usually the "elbow" in the curve.

- In our instance, the elbow appears to be around 3 to 4 k clusters.

#### Average Silhouette Method

```{r}
fviz_nbclust(X_matrix_cluster, kmeans, method = "silhouette")
```

- Measures how well each point lies within a cluster, in this case it suggests 2 clusters.

- 3 or 4.

- High average silhouette width = good clustering

- Average silhouette method computes the average silhouette of observations for different values of k.

```{r}
set.seed(1234)

km_fit_3 <- kmeans(X_matrix_cluster_km, centers = 3, nstart = 20)
km_fit_4 <- kmeans(X_matrix_cluster_km, centers = 4, nstart = 20)
km_fit_5 <- kmeans(X_matrix_cluster_km, centers = 5, nstart = 20)
```

- nstart = 20: Chosen over a lower value as a undesirable local optimum may be obtained.

```{r}
# inspect cluster labels
table(km_fit_3$cluster)
table(km_fit_4$cluster)
table(km_fit_5$cluster)
```

```{r}
# inspect cluster centroids
#km_fit$centers
```

## 6. Plot clusters

```{r}
p1 <- fviz_cluster(km_fit_3,
             data = X_matrix_cluster_km,
             geom = "point",
             ellipse.type = "convex",
             ggtheme = theme_bw()
             ) + ggtitle("k = 3")
p2 <- fviz_cluster(km_fit_4,
                   data = X_matrix_cluster_km,
                   geom = "point",
                   ellipse.type = "convex",
                   ggtheme = theme_bw()
                   ) + ggtitle("k = 4")
p3 <- fviz_cluster(km_fit_5,
                   data = X_matrix_cluster_km,
                   geom = "point",
                   ellipse.type = "convex",
                   ggtheme = theme_bw()
                   ) + ggtitle("k = 5")
```

```{r}
# combine and compare plots of clusters

grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, nrow = 2)

```

- Plot interpretation:

  - As our data includes more than 2 variables, the function performs principal component analysis (PCA) and plots the data points according to the first 2 principal components that explain majority of the variance.

#### Evaluate the effectiveness of the clustering using Silhouette Score

```{r}
# Silhouette scores
sil_3 <- silhouette(km_fit_3$cluster, d_mat)
sil_4 <- silhouette(km_fit_4$cluster, d_mat)
sil_5 <- silhouette(km_fit_5$cluster, d_mat)
  
# Avg silhouette width
avg_sil_width_3 <- mean(sil_3[, "sil_width"])
avg_sil_width_4 <- mean(sil_4[, "sil_width"])
avg_sil_width_5 <- mean(sil_5[, "sil_width"])

cat("Silhouette Score (k = 3): ", avg_sil_width_3, "\n")
cat("Silhouette Score (k = 4): ", avg_sil_width_4, "\n")
cat("Silhouette Score (k = 5): ", avg_sil_width_5)
```

- A higher average silhouette width is better, as it represents the effectiveness of our clustering

- Silhouette Score (k = 3): 0.3231498

- Silhouette Score (k = 4): 0.2551525

- Silhouette Score (k = 5): 0.2029958

### 6.1 Apply clusters to data

```{r}
# Assign cluster IDs - KMeans
cadia$kmeans_id_5 <- km_fit$cluster
```

```{r}
names(cadia)
```

```{r}
nrow(cadia)
length(km_fit$cluster)

table(cadia$kmeans_id_5)
```

### 6.2 Export for ArcGIS

```{r}
write.csv(cadia, "cadia_kmeans_5.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# Peru, 2019

## **1. Prepare data**

```{r}
# Prep data

peru_failed <- read_excel("2019_Cobriza_Peru_Failed.xlsx")

str(peru_failed)
head(peru_failed)
dim(peru_failed)
names(peru_failed)
```

```{r}
# unfailed

peru_unfailed <- read_excel("2019_Cobriza_Peru_Unfailed.xlsx")

str(peru_unfailed)
head(peru_unfailed)
dim(peru_unfailed)
names(peru_unfailed)
```

```{r}
# Extract displacement columns - FAILED
d_cols_peru_F <- grep("^D_", names(peru_failed), value = TRUE)
length(d_cols_peru_F)
head(d_cols_peru_F)

peru_dis_F <- peru_failed[, d_cols_peru_F]

head(peru_dis_F)

dim(peru_dis_F)

# Check for missing vals

sum(is.na(peru_dis_F))
```

```{r}
# Extract displacement columns - UNFAILED
d_cols_peru_U <- grep("^D_", names(peru_unfailed), value = TRUE)
length(d_cols_peru_U)
head(d_cols_peru_U)

peru_dis_U <- peru_unfailed[, d_cols_peru_U]

head(peru_dis_U)

dim(peru_dis_U)

# Check for missing vals

sum(is.na(peru_dis_U))
```

## **2. Convert to matrix**

```{r}
# Matrix - FAILED

peru_dis_F_matrix <- as.matrix(peru_dis_F)

sum(is.na(peru_dis_F_matrix))
```

```{r}
# Matrix - UNFAILED

peru_dis_U_matrix <- as.matrix(peru_dis_U)

sum(is.na(peru_dis_U_matrix))
```

- Remove baseline date

```{r}
# baseline date = 1st column

col_sd_p_F <- apply(peru_dis_F_matrix, 2, sd)

which(col_sd_p_F == 0)

col_sd_p_U <- apply(peru_dis_U_matrix, 2, sd)

which(col_sd_p_U == 0)
```

```{r}
# Remove first column (0 = baseline date of cumulative displacement)

zero_cols_F <- colnames(peru_dis_F_matrix)[col_sd_p_F == 0]
zero_cols_F

peru_dis_F_matrix_cluster <- peru_dis_F_matrix[, col_sd_p_F > 0, drop = FALSE]
```

```{r}
zero_cols_U <- colnames(peru_dis_U_matrix)[col_sd_p_U == 0]
zero_cols_U

peru_dis_U_matrix_cluster <- peru_dis_U_matrix[, col_sd_p_U > 0, drop = FALSE]
```

## **3. Compute distance matrix**

```{r}
# Distance Matrix
# distance measure: for now Euclidean
      # test against others later

d_mat_peru_F <- dist(peru_dis_F_matrix_cluster, method = "euclidean")
```

```{r}
# Distance Matrix
# distance measure: for now Euclidean
# test against others later

d_mat_peru_U <- dist(peru_dis_U_matrix_cluster, method = "euclidean")
```

4.  Hierarchical clustering (Ward linkage)

```{r}

hclust_peru_F <- hclust(d_mat_peru_F, method="ward.D2")
```

```{r}

hclust_peru_U <- hclust(d_mat_peru_U, method="ward.D2")
```

- Dendrogram

```{r}
plot(hclust_peru_F, labels = FALSE)
```

```{r}
plot(hclust_peru_U, labels = FALSE)
```

- Based on both dendrograms, splits at k = 3, k = 4, and k = 5 may be tested.

## **4. Assign clusters and Export for ArcGIS**

```{r}
# Failed
peru_failed$hc_3 <- cutree(hclust_peru_F, k = 3)
peru_failed$hc_4 <- cutree(hclust_peru_F, k = 4)
peru_failed$hc_5 <- cutree(hclust_peru_F, k = 5)
```

```{r}
# Unfailed
peru_unfailed$hc_3 <- cutree(hclust_peru_U, k = 3)
peru_unfailed$hc_4 <- cutree(hclust_peru_U, k = 4)
peru_unfailed$hc_5 <- cutree(hclust_peru_U, k = 5)
```

```{r}
# check sizes
nrow(peru_failed)
length(peru_failed$hc_3)

nrow(peru_unfailed)
length(peru_unfailed$hc_3)
```

```{r}
# inspect cluster sizes

table(peru_failed$hc_3)
table(peru_failed$hc_4)
table(peru_failed$hc_5)

table(peru_unfailed$hc_3)
table(peru_unfailed$hc_4)
table(peru_unfailed$hc_5)
```

```{r}
write.csv(peru_failed, "peru_failed_hierarchical_clusters.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
write.csv(peru_unfailed, "peru_unfailed_hierarchical_clusters.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```


Average Silhouette Method

